Let’s find out about the Irish who lived just south of the river Thames.
Their story and achievements, covering the last few centuries to recent times, incorporating local London history whilst strolling through beautiful historic parks and Georgian squares. Starts outside The Tankard pub, Kennington Road. SE11. Finishing at Kennington Park. SE11.

images.title: Irish Stories South of the River

properties.name: Irish Stories South of the River

properties.description: Obra is Sordo Madaleno’s transdisciplinary laboratory, open library, and public living room, turning our London studio into a public-facing space for curiosity, testing, and dialogue. An addition to London's architectural landscape, Obra will host temporary exhibitions, events, and talks fostering exchange between the studio, the environments it works within, and the communities it engages.
properties.name: Obra

properties.description: An interactive print making workshop exploring the threshold between public and gallery space through exchange and collection. Using the gallery hatch, visitors are invited to transform found ephemera into printed artworks. Inspired by the exhibiting artists' practices, the workshop playfully turns the gallery into a machine for making art, reimagining the traces of everyday life in Hackney.
properties.name: Print Portal

properties.description:
Lisson Grove Studios is a 1088m2 mixed use creative workspace hub providing permanent, affordable workspace for artists, designers, makers and small creative businesses.

The complex opened in February 2026 and includes 38 creative enterprise studios, a café, dance & rehearsal studio, 22 desk spaces, a meeting room, two phone booths and an exhibition space, arranged over 5 split level floors.
properties.name: Lisson Grove Studios

properties.description:
A unique immersive theatre space in Wembley.

Punchdrunk Enrichment creates immersive theatre experiences for families, schools and communities. Through our adventurous, high-quality approach to storytelling we champion the imagination.
At our creative home in Brent we run family theatre shows, community days, masterclasses and more. Come and explore!
properties.name: Punchdrunk Enrichment Stores

properties.description: A creatively refurbished family home showcasing sustainable reuse and handmade ceramics. Reclaimed cupboards, salvaged furniture and broken tiles have been transformed into bespoke kitchens, bathrooms and mosaics. Handmade ceramic sinks, lamps, tiles and decorative objects are integrated throughout the house, creating a unique interior where craft, sustainability and everyday living come together.
properties.name: Windermere av, Merton

properties.description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.
properties.name: Green Lodge

properties.description: We would like to welcome the local community to join with us to celebrate being 150 years old this year.  Inside you'll be able to see a timeline of the Church's history, including its role in the community, and other displays. Tours of the worship space and the crypt will be available.

properties.description: On Sat 12th Sep, the church is holding it's annual 'Big Green Fair' and planning to open the balcony, sanctuary and chancel for tours of the mosaics, vestments and frontals to offer a fuller experience of the treasures of the church. There will be food, music and workshops on the day and we will run photography and paper airplane competitions on the balcony (not normally open to the public).

properties.description: A family home with a newly created living space with dramatic changes in height and subtly defined nooks and zones supporting contemporary family life. Punctured openings create new connections and viewpoints between and through the new spaces. These openings are highlighted in a bold, bright ultramarine blue that contrasts with the earthy palette of other new and redefined elements.
properties.name: Peek-a-Blue

properties.description:
West Ham pumping station was built to raise
West Ham sewage to the level of Sir Joseph
Bazalgette's Northern Outfall sewer (1864)
along which it could then flow under gravity
to Beckton works for treatment.
Contains two unique Lilleshall beam steam engines.
Also once a power station to power the Westham Corpration Tramways

images.title: Photo of West Ham Pumping Station
Photo of West Ham Pumping Station

properties.name: West Ham Pumping Station

properties.description: A Great Fire Survivor, damaged in the blitz, the post war restoration of this fascinating building began 75 years ago this year.  Described by John Betjeman as a 'country church in the world of Seething Lane' the building uniquely blends medieval fabric with Festival of Britain era motifs. Explore the medieval crypt, 'Pepys' vestry, church tower and ringing room. Bellringing demonstrations.
properties.name: St Olave Hart Street

properties.description: Founded in 1891, Royal Trinity Hospice is the oldest hospice in the UK, set within a terrace of listed Georgian houses overlooking Clapham Common and surrounded by landscaped gardens. Join us for a guided tour around the hospice and grounds, including areas of interest usually not open for visitors.
properties.name: Royal Trinity Hospice and grounds

properties.description: Turning what was once a backland site into a two-storey, two-bedroom detached home, Wade House introduces a modern new-build to the heart of Metroland.
properties.name: Wade House

properties.description: Renovated by Fynn Architects, this early Victorian flat in the Barnsbury Conservation Area has been reconfigured for a young family. The previous layout left the kitchen stranded in a cramped, pokey room at the rear, so the project brings it forward into the front room and reworks the layout around how the family actually lives, adding a new WC and a nursery for the new arrival.
properties.name: Barnsbury Flat

properties.description: Discover the architectural and civic history of Hillingdon Civic Centre on a guided tour led by local history and architecture experts. Explore its distinctive design and incorporation of the old tow, marriage room, public artworks, stained glass,  iconic "Bones" artwork, Lady Hillingdon portrait and Jane Grey window, revealing how this landmark reflects Hillingdon's heritage, identity and growth.
properties.name: Hillingdon Civic Centre

properties.description: The Avery Hill Winter Garden is a remarkable Victorian glasshouse set within the historic Avery Hill estate in southeast London. Built in the late 19th century, it was once home to an extensive collection of exotic plants and remains one of London’s largest surviving Victorian winter gardens.

properties.description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
properties.name: Southlands Arts Centre

properties.description: Be inspired by Croydon's space age buildings and aviation history - from Apollo and Lunar House, to Croydon Airport. Build your own models of familiar buildings redesigned as spacecrafts and transform the town centre into a space station.

properties.description: As part of the weekend event Build /  Play / Shape Croydon, MATT+FIONA will lead a collaborative cardboard-build activity inspired by landmarks from Croydon's skyline. properties.description: Behind the façade of power of Westminster lies a maze of backstreets, brimming with history from a medieval English village, prisons, slums, plague pits to birth of English printing and world of espionage… Trace the footsteps of suffragette and spies, and uncover the fascinating stories, people and events shaped British history.

We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.
properties.name: Southbank Printmakers

Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
properties.name: Ongéan

properties.description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
properties.name: Corbett Community Library

properties.description: A special exhibition exploring the people and places that shaped the area during the Second World War. Tracing famous figures who made Soho their home, and the ordinary everyday heroes who kept the area functioning and our spirits up!
properties.name: The West End At War

properties.description:
Step back in time with a guided walk around the historic Excalibur Estate, the UK's largest surviving post-war prefabricated housing estate.

Discover why these remarkable homes were built in the aftermath of the Second World War, explore their innovative design and architecture, and hear the stories of the people who have made Excalibur their home over the decades.
properties.name: Prefab Walking Tour - Excalibur Estate

properties.description:
A walk round Somers Town by locals founders  of a museum to preserve an area that feels at risk of extinction.

A Space for Us – People’s Museum Somers Town is a space to preserve local voice and the area; to celebrate an incredible ‘radical, reformers and uncommon people’s‘ histories, to record the change now, as well as to campaign and preserve local working class heritage.
properties.name: Somers Town - Photo walk

properties.description: Bridge House is a mixed-use building by Studioshaw with 40 apartments and commercial space. The design is a new vernacular for multi-unit residential development in London. All apartments are dual-aspect and share a rooftop garden, with balconies over the canal and new public square. The facade is made from concrete elements cast only 750m from site. The building's structure is its architecture.

properties.description:
Lewisham Heritage is responsible for the collection, preservation and making available the history and heritage for Lewisham Council and its communities.
While Lewisham Library is being refurbished our Heritage Reading Room is located at Catford Library.

There will be a display of archive material in Meeting Room 2 and hourly tours of the Heritage Reading Room.
properties.name: Lewisham Heritage at Catford Library

properties.description:
An original walking trail set to a celebratory soundtrack:
uncovering lively tales of secret doors, latest crazes and 300 years of entertaining Soho- from Georgian masquerades to the beat of the present day. 
A collaboration between the Museum of Soho and site-responsive, immersive theatre makers Gideon Reeling, blending digital tech with performance

images.title: Photo of Gideon Reeling’s The Soho Shuffle
Photo of Gideon Reeling’s The Soho Shuffle

properties.name: Gideon Reeling’s The Soho Shuffle

properties.description: Join Maccreanor Lavington for a walking tour of two of the first residential buildings to be delivered at Brent Cross Town – The Delamarre and Conductor House. The buildings form an important part of the emerging new town and demonstrate how high-quality architecture landscape and public realm can come together to create a distinctive and welcoming neighbourhood.
properties.name: The Delamarre & Conductor House, Brent Cross Town Tour

properties.description: The building has had many incarnations since its construction in the 1890s as a woolen warehouse.   It became a home to the Italian Benevolent Society, then a fascist club, a serviceman's club, and now a library with the largest publicly accessible collection of Chinese language books in the UK.
properties.name: Charing Cross Library

properties.description:
Ever wondered just what makes a building interesting, characterful and joyful? It’s not just a vague sensation or an indescribable feeling. There are specific things you can look for.

Explore the buildings around you using the Humanise Spotter’s Guide, a mobile-friendly guide which invites you to look more closely at the buildings around us, and think about how they’re shaping how we all feel.
properties.name: Humanise Spotters Guide: King's Cross
